speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies.

Although the scraping was negative, the clinical presentation of intense itching and red bumps on the thigh is highly suggestive of scabies, which can sometimes be missed in initial tests due to low sensitivity or early presentation. The recent travel to a conference may have facilitated exposure, and the distribution of lesions on the thigh is a common site. Given the strong clinical suspicion despite the negative scraping, I recommend starting treatment with permethrin 5% cream.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies
